teachings.teaching: Uddalaka tells his son Shvetaketu that by knowing one lump of clay, everything made of clay is known. The different shapes are names. What is real in all of them is the clay.
teachings.link: In a reaction the atoms stay and only their arrangement changes. Chemistry adds one thing that the verse does not say. The new arrangement really behaves in a new way, because curds do not act like milk.
verse: यथा सोम्यैकेन मृत्पिण्डेन सर्वं मृन्मयं विज्ञातं स्यात्

teachings.teaching: The Buddha teaches that all things that are put together are impermanent.
teachings.link: Every substance in this unit could be changed by some reaction. Even a hard plaster wall is slowly joining with carbon dioxide from the air.

science.text: In a chemical reaction no atom is made or lost. Lavoisier showed this in the 1780s by weighing reactions in sealed vessels.
Chemists can now follow a bond as it breaks, using laser flashes far shorter than a billionth of a second. Ahmed Zewail won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1999 for this work.
Some scientists think that life began as reactions that kept each other going, before there were any cells.

other_view.who: Many chemists who teach and predict reactions
other_view.view: The kinds are more than names. A joining and a swapping behave differently, and knowing the kind tells you what the products will be. It is true that every reaction is bonds breaking and forming. But that is too general to help anyone at the laboratory bench.

practice.title: One breath, one reaction
practice.say: Sit still and breathe in slowly. The oxygen in this breath will react with food inside your cells. Hold it for a count of three. Now breathe out slowly on to your palm. Your breath is warm and damp. The warmth, the water and the carbon dioxide were made by reactions in your cells. Do this five times, and notice each breath going in and coming out.
practice.kid: Breathe in slowly. This oxygen will react with your food. Count to three. Breathe out on to your palm. Is your breath warm and damp? Reactions in your cells made that. Do it five times.

ask: The calcium in a shell becomes lime, then plaster on a wall, then stone again. Is it the same thing all the way through?
If every reaction is bonds breaking and bonds forming, why do curds, flames and rust look so different?
The atoms in your body change partners every second. What stays the same in you?

playtest: Every experiment, activity, game and challenge was reasoned through step by step for a city flat. The reasoning used the chemistry and the usual kitchen amounts. None of them has been tried at home yet, so treat the times and amounts as a first guide. Second Squeeze (core) needs 300 millilitres of milk and about 3 lemons. 200 millilitres of milk usually curdles with 2 to 4 teaspoons of lemon juice. Milks and lemons differ, so the steps say to count and record. The whey test works only while the whey is still warm. Tumbler B is expected to stop making curds after 2 to 6 tablespoons of milk. This number is the least certain in the unit. If the whey is heated almost to boiling, a few very fine flecks may appear in tumbler A. They are another milk protein, and the whey should not be reheated. The Pan and the Lid (core) needs cooking soda, a dry pan and three cold steel lids. A grown-up does the heating. The empty-pan step matters, because it shows that the drops come from the powder. The heated powder is washing soda and must not be tasted. Powder and Water needs plaster of Paris, which a hardware or stationery shop sells cheaply. With 6 tablespoons the warmth is gentle, so the child compares the two cups with the same hand. Soap and Sour needs a true soap bar. Some bathing bars are not soap, and they will not turn milky. Hard tap water also makes soap cloudy, so the step says to use filtered or boiled water. Will It Burn uses a candle and must be done by a grown-up near an open window. Salt colours the flame yellow, and the candle leaves soot on the spoon. Neither is burning. If all four plates are kept, Four Plates needs 3 rajma, 11 white chana, 10 moong, a groundnut and a peppercorn. The card game has 24 cards and plays well alone. The Sharpest Coin Print needs three coins of the same kind. No part needs a garden or an animal. Softened: Proust's work is now dated to the 1790s, and the shop prices are removed. Still simplified: the account of milk (how casein clusters are built is still debated), and soap is treated as one substance. The verses and the fragment of Empedocles are paraphrases.
